Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.

We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Account Executive, Card Plastics

What does a successful Account Executive, Card Plastics do at Fiserv?

As a successful Account Executive, Card Plastics, you will own and grow a portfolio of existing clients within an assigned territory. You will build trusted relationships, understand each client’s business priorities, and proactively prospect across assigned accounts to uncover, develop, and close new plastics, personalization, and digital opportunities. This role is centered on client retention, relationship expansion, and increasing Fiserv’s share of wallet.

What you will do:

  • Own and manage relationships across an assigned portfolio of existing clients and serve as a trusted advisor for their card plastics, personalization, and digital needs
  • Develop and execute territory and account plans that prioritize high-potential clients, retention risks, key decision-makers, and growth opportunities
  • Prospect within assigned client accounts to identify unmet needs, new buying centers, and opportunities to expand Fiserv’s products and services
  • Build strong relationships with C-suite, operational leaders, and day-to-day client contacts to understand business goals, card strategies, inventory needs, and buying cycles
  • Use client data, order history, inventory trends, market insights, and competitive intelligence to create targeted upsell, cross-sell and conversion opportunities
  • Lead the sales process from discovery through proposal, pricing, negotiation, and close while ensuring a positive client experience
  • Drive growth through new card programs, product upgrades, card redesigns, material changes, contactless adoption, personalization services, and other value-added solutions
  • Partner with Relationship Managers, service, product, operations, inside sales, and other internal teams to deliver coordinated solutions and resolve barriers to growth
  • Support client retention by proactively addressing business needs, coordinating contract renewals, and escalating risks when appropriate
  • Maintain an accurate pipeline, forecast revenue, document client activity, and update opportunities and next steps in CRM
  • Meet or exceed growth, renewal, pipeline, activity, and client engagement goals for the assigned territory

What you will need to have:

  • 5+ years of successful sales, account management, or client relationship experience in the payments or financial services industry
  • Demonstrated ability to grow revenue within existing accounts through consultative selling, prospecting, upselling, and cross-selling
  • Experience developing relationships and effectively communicating with client stakeholders at all levels, including executive management
  • Ability to manage a territory, prioritize a portfolio of accounts, and advance multiple opportunities through the sales cycle
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of experience, education, and/or military service

What would be great to have:

  • Experience managing and growing a portfolio of existing card plastics, payments, or financial services clients
  • Familiarity with Fiserv issuer and Output Solutions offerings
  • Knowledge of card manufacturing, personalization, inventory planning, contactless migration, and related industry trends
  • Experience collaborating across relationship management, product, service, operations, and sales support teams
  • Experience using CRM systems to manage pipelines, forecast revenue, and track account activity

Important information about this role:

  • Ability to travel up to 30%

You must currently possess valid and unrestricted U.S. work authorization to be considered for this role. Individuals with temporary visas including, but not limited to, F-1 (OPT, CPT, STEM), H-1B, H-2, or TN, or any candidate requiring sponsorship, now or in the future, will not be considered for this role.

Salary Range:

$54,500.00-$85,250.00

These pay ranges apply to employees in Maryland. Pay ranges for employees in other states may differ. Certain Positions are Commissions eligible.

It is unlawful to discriminate against a prospective employee due to the individual's status as a veteran.

Thank you for considering employment with Fiserv. Please:

  • Apply using your legal name
  • Complete the step-by-step profile and attach your resume (either is acceptable, both are preferable).

Our commitment to Equal Opportunity:

Fiserv is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other category protected by law.

If you have a disability and require a reasonable accommodation in completing a job application or otherwise participating in the overall hiring process, please contact . Please note our AskHR representatives do not have visibility to your application status. Current associates who require a workplace accommodation should refer to Fiserv’s Disability Accommodation Policy for additional information.

Note to agencies:

Fiserv does not accept resume submissions from agencies outside of existing agreements. Please do not send resumes to Fiserv associates. Fiserv is not responsible for any fees associated with unsolicited resume submissions.

Warning about fake job posts:

Please be aware of fraudulent job postings that are not affiliated with Fiserv. Principal Polymer Processing Engineer

Injection Molding

Location: Largo, FL (Remote)
Department: Engineering / Operations
Job Category: Engineering
Career Track: Individual Contributor
Job Profile: Principal Engineer
Reports To: Sr. Director Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
FLSA Status: Exempt

***This position is not eligible for employer-based sponsorship***


Position Summary

The Principal Polymer Processing Engineer is a recognized technical expert responsible for advancing injection molding capabilities, polymer processing technologies, and manufacturing performance across CONMED. This role provides technical leadership for the plastic parts design geometry for injection molding manufacturability; for new injection molds design conceptualization, manufacturing and performance testing; for the plastic injection molding cell equipment selection and performance testing; for the plastic injection molding process optimization and qualification; and for the sustaining support of the plastic injection molding process and mold’s production life cycle maintenance for plastic parts used to manufacture medical devices and components. Working across Engineering, Operations, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and external partners, the Principal Polymer Processing Engineer leads highly complex technical initiatives from concept through commercialization and ongoing production. The individual serves as a trusted technical advisor, applying advanced engineering judgment to solve critical processing challenges; establishing technical standards; reducing manufacturing risk; and improving product quality, cost, capacity and reliability.


This is an individual-contributor position that leads through technical expertise, influence, and cross-functional collaboration rather than direct people management.


Key Responsibilities


Technical Leadership and Process Development

  • Serve as a Technical Advisor to Sourcing and Quality in custom molders facilities; molding cells equipment; injection molding process optimization and troubleshooting; mold design and manufacturing; mold preventive maintenance, troubleshooting and tooling engineering; metrology and MSA; and quality engineering technical capacities & capabilities assessment, and periodic audits.
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert in part design conceptualization for injection molding manufacturability; injection molding process optimization; injection molding process engineering (troubleshooting); mold design concept optimization; and mold tooling engineering (troubleshooting).
  • Lead the development, optimization, qualification and validation of complex injection molding processes, equipment, molds and supporting technologies.
  • Establish robust processing strategies based on polymer science, material characteristics, part design, mold design, equipment capability, and intended product requirements.
  • Apply scientific molding principles and structured experimentation to define processing windows and ensure repeatable, capable, and controlled manufacturing processes.
  • Provide technical direction for challenging molding applications involving tight tolerances, complex geometries, engineered resins, high-performance polymers, multi-material components, insert molding, overmolding, or other specialized processes.
  • Evaluate emerging polymer-processing technologies and recommend investments that support product innovation, manufacturing capability, capacity, quality, and long-term business needs.
  • Develop and maintain technical standards, engineering practices, design guidelines, specifications, and process-development methodologies.
  • Translate complex technical information into clear recommendations for engineering, operations, and business leadership.

New Product and Technology Development

  • Partner with R&D, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, Operations, and Supply Chain to support new product development and product-transfer activities.
  • Provide design-for-manufacturability guidance related to polymer selection, molded-part design geometry, tooling strategy, tolerances, gating, cooling, shrinkage, warpage, and process capability.
  • Lead or provide technical oversight for mold-flow analysis; tool design reviews; mold manufacturing and performance testing; process characterization; equipment selection and performance testing; and manufacturing-readiness assessments.
  • Identify technical risks early in the development process and establish appropriate mitigation plans.
  • Lead the transition of injection-molded products and processes from development through validation, commercialization, and sustained production.
  • Define critical process parameters and support the development of appropriate inspection, monitoring, and control strategies.
  • Ensure that technical decisions balance product performance, patient and user needs, compliance, manufacturability, cost, capacity, and business continuity.

Process Validation and Compliance

  • Provide technical leadership for mold bench assembly and functional performance assessment; mold installation qualification; molding cell equipment assessment and performance testing; mold dry cycling, mold first out-of-tool and mold functional performance testing; molding process characterization and optimization; plastic forming steel compliance assessment and, if applicable, tweaking (grooming); mold operational qualification; and mold performance qualification activities.
  • Develop or approve technical protocols, reports, engineering studies, acceptance criteria, statistical analyses, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure polymer-processing activities comply with applicable quality-system requirements, engineering standards, regulatory expectations, and internal procedures.
  • Support risk-management activities, including process FMEAs, design FMEAs, control plans, process-risk assessments, and technical investigations.
  • Partner with Quality Engineering to establish effective process controls and ensure sustained process capability.
  • Provide technical support during internal audits, external audits, regulatory inspections, and customer inquiries, as needed.

Manufacturing and Business Performance

  • Lead the resolution of complex or recurring molding process and/or tooling issues affecting safety, quality, delivery, capacity, cost, or customer service.
  • Apply structured problem-solving methods and advanced data analysis to identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Improve manufacturing performance through cycle-time reduction, scrap reduction, yield improvement, process-capability improvement, automation, tooling optimization, and material utilization.
  • Develop solutions that increase process reliability, reduce variation, and improve overall equipment and operational effectiveness.
  • Assess existing molding equipment, auxiliary systems, tooling, and processes to identify capability gaps, obsolescence risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Support capital-equipment selection, technical justification, supplier evaluation, installation, qualification, and production implementation.
  • Provide technical leadership for design changes, material changes, product transfers, process transfers, supplier transitions, capacity expansion, and manufacturing-network initiatives.
  • Develop business cases and recommendations supported by technical evidence, risk assessment, financial impact, and implementation requirements.

Technical Influence and Collaboration

  • Act as a technical consultant to engineering teams, operations leaders, project teams, and senior leadership.
  • Lead cross-functional technical initiatives that may span multiple products, departments, suppliers, or manufacturing locations.
  • Influence decisions where technical complexity, business risk, or organizational impact is significant.
  • Build effective partnerships with equipment manufacturers, toolmakers, resin suppliers, contract manufacturers, consultants, and other external technical resources.
  • Represent manufacturing and polymer-processing considerations in product, technology, and business-planning discussions.
  • Facilitate technical reviews and ensure decisions, actions, risks, and accountabilities are clearly documented.
  • Communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical audiences at all levels of the organization.

Knowledge Development and Mentoring

  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to engineers, technicians, molders, and other manufacturing professionals.
  • Build organizational capability by sharing specialized knowledge, developing technical training, and establishing repeatable engineering methods.
  • Review and provide guidance on the technical work of other engineers without serving as their direct manager.
  • Promote disciplined experimentation, fact-based decision making, continuous improvement, and strong engineering practices.
  • Maintain current knowledge of developments in polymer science, molding technology, manufacturing systems, medical-device requirements, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute to the development of CONMED’s long-term polymer-processing and manufacturing-technology roadmap.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Polymer Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Science, or closely related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving injection molding, polymer processing, plastics manufacturing, tooling, or closely related manufacturing technologies.
  • 2 years of experience applying technical knowledge and expertise troubleshooting injection molded parts noncompliance opportunities to determine whether root cause is part design geometry, raw material, raw material handling, molding process, mold steel dimensions, mold steel wear, mold design conceptualization, molding cell selection, molding cell functional performance, part’s inspection method, inspection fixture, inspection equipment, parts conveying, parts packaging design, parts storing and/or part’s transit related.
  • 2 years of experience leading complex technical projects and influencing decisions across multiple functions. Experience developing or reviewing engineering protocols, validation documents, technical reports, specifications, risk assessments, and process documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or doctorate in Polymer Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline.
  • Experience in a regulated medical-device, pharmaceutical, life-sciences, automotive, aerospace, or similarly controlled manufacturing environment.
  • Experience with injection molding of medical-device components or other high-precision, high-reliability products.
  • Working knowledge of applicable FDA quality-system requirements, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, good manufacturing practices, and process-validation expectations.
  • Expertise in one or more specialized processes, such as insert molding, overmolding, micro-molding, multi-shot molding, silicone molding, high-temperature materials, or bio-compatible polymers.
  • Experience with mold-flow simulation and analysis tools.
  • Experience with automation, in-mold sensing, process-monitoring systems, machine connectivity, or advanced manufacturing controls.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or structured problem-solving certification.
  • Experience supporting manufacturing transfers, supplier development, capacity expansion, or global operations.
  • Experience working with toolmakers, resin suppliers, equipment manufacturers, and contract manufacturers.
  • Experience with mold design conceptualization, mold manufacturing, mold functional performance testing and mold predictive and preventive maintenance programs.
  • Demonstrated expertise in injection molding process development, optimization, validation and troubleshooting assessment; and in mold design conceptualization, performance testing, plastic forming steel compliance, grooming activities, and troubleshooting assessment.
  • Advanced knowledge of thermoplastic materials, polymer behavior, resin handling, drying, rheology, shrinkage, warpage, degradation, and material-process interactions.
  • Demonstrated experience applying scientific molding principles, design of experiments, statistical analysis, process-capability methods, and structured root-cause analysis.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently define problems, evaluate technical alternatives, and deliver sustainable solutions to highly complex engineering challenges.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and technical documentation skills.



***This position is not eligible for employer based sponsorship***

Summary This position is responsible for identifying product requirements and driving technology development projects related to business growth of thermoplastic elastomer (TPE) compounds. Requirements include strong plastics and/or rubber materials and technology skills and, excellent skills in customer relationships, business development, project management, teamwork, organization, and communication. This person is the materials subject matter expert for the customer-facing team.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Responsible for managing development activities associated with TPE materials.
  • Pursues new business opportunities through diligent customer and market development efforts:
    • Identifies strategic markets and customers;
    • Determines material requirements and specifications for targeted applications;
    • Collaborates with Audia Elastomers product development engineers to develop material solutions to meet customer needs;
    • Interprets sample results and provides data sheets and other material physical property information to customers;
    • Coordinates and attends customer molding trials as necessary, providing feedback to product development regarding direction of future work;
    • Presents a formalized data package of developed material(s) for customer approval(s).
  • Interfaces with converters, Tiers, and OEMs to achieve and document Audia Elastomers product approvals.
  • May support non-automotive applications in the given geography where expertise allows, and/or where a converter serves multiple market segments.
  • Effectively promotes Audia Elastomers products and organizational capabilities.
  • Submits call reports and monthly activity summaries concerning customer-related activities as requested by manager.
  • Provides timely response to customer inquiries and complaints to ensure customer satisfaction.
  • Performs other duties and assignments as directed by manager.
  • Performs all duties safely and in compliance with documentation outlined in the Safety, Health & Environmental and defined quality management systems.

Recommended Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in engineering, science, or equivalent, and/or 5-7 years of experience with elastomeric (preferred) or plastic (acceptable) materials in the automotive industry
  • Demonstrated ability to leverage technical strength to develop new business.
  • Ability to build and maintain strong, long-term customer relationships.
  • Ability to work seamlessly with commercial and product development teams to develop appropriate strategies to address customer and/or market need(s).
  • Excellent communication skills, self-starter, sense of urgency, personable, and well organized.
  • Skilled in the use of basic computer software, including word-processing and spreadsheets.
  • Self-sufficient in terms of time management and support.

Working Conditions

  • Environment – Commercial and/or home office as appropriate.
  • Travel – Frequent travel, generally over 50% and can include international travel.

Responsibility for Safety, Health & Environmental

  • Individual is expected to perform job duties safely and in compliance with documentation outlined in the Safety, Health & Environmental system.

Responsibility for Quality

Individual is expected to perform job duties in compliance with defined management system requirements

About the Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented and technically skilled Packaging Engineer to join our team. This role is responsible for designing, developing, and qualifying packaging solutions for our hair care product portfolio from initial concept through commercialization. You will work cross-functionally with R&D, product development, procurement, manufacturing, and marketing teams to ensure packaging is functional, compatible with formulas, cost-effective, and can be manufactured to scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop primary and secondary packaging components (bottles, closures, pumps, tubes, jars) for new and existing hair care products.
  • Oversee compatibility testing between formulations and packaging materials to ensure product stability and shelf-life integrity.
  • Create and maintain technical packaging specifications, drawings, and documentation.
  • Partners with suppliers and vendors to source materials, negotiate specifications, and resolve technical issues.
  • Support tooling development and manage the engineering change process for new molds and components.
  • Perform or coordinate functional testing (drop tests, torque testing, leak testing, environmental/stability testing) and analyze results. Troubleshoot packaging defects and manufacturing line issues; drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with formulation and product development teams to align packaging with product claims, aesthetics, and brand requirements.
  • Support sustainability initiatives, including recyclable/PCR material integration and packaging weight reduction.
  • Manage project timelines for packaging development and execution, ensuring on-time delivery for product launches. Supports Supply Chain team with ongoing packaging support and supplier relationships.
  • Ensure all packaging complies with regulatory, safety, and quality standards.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Packaging Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, or related field
  • 3+ years of experience in packaging development, preferably within cosmetics, personal care, or CPG industries
  • Working knowledge of plastics, materials science, and manufacturing processes (injection molding, blow molding, extrusion)
  • Familiarity with packaging testing protocols, quality standards and designing pallet patterns.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work cross-functionally with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including developing and managing Supplier relationships.

Preferred:

  • Experience specifically with hair care, skin care, or liquid/viscous product packaging
  • Knowledge of sustainable packaging materials and design-for-recyclability principles
  • Experience working directly with contract manufacturers or co-packers
  • Familiarity with FDA/regulatory requirements for cosmetic packaging

About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable -- turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

As a Mechanical Engineer, you will own the design, analysis, and validation of the structural and kinematic systems that make Asimov move. You will take components from concept through production-ready hardware -- working across joints, actuators, enclosures, and structural members -- ensuring every design holds up mechanically and integrates cleanly with the broader electromechanical system.

What You'll Do

  • Design and develop mechanical assemblies across the full humanoid body, including joints, actuators, sensor mounts, and structural members

  • Develop detailed 3D part, drawings and assembly models across plastics, metal, and composite materials in Solidworks or equivalent CAD tools

  • Run hands-on test rigs: load testing, fatigue cycling, thermal soak, and kinematic validation across body segments

  • Execute DFM reviews alongside contract manufacturers, going to the floor to understand tooling constraints, cycle times, and failure modes firsthand

  • Create and maintain production drawings with GD&T and inspection callouts for handoff to CMs and QA

  • Set up and instrument test stands, wire sensors, and collect data to analyze failure modes and close the loop on design iterations

  • Work across plastics, metals, and composites, selecting materials and joining methods appropriate for the loading conditions and production intent

  • Coordinate with firmware and electrical teams to physically integrate actuators, sensors, and PCBs into mechanical assemblies, ensuring cable routing, connector access, and serviceability are accounted for

  • Contribute to Menlo's open-source hardware releases, including build guides, BOM documentation, and assembly instructions for the communityContribute to Menlo's open-source design efforts, including CAD releases, manufacturing documentation, and build guides for the broader robotics community

What You'll Bring

  • 3 or more years of hands-on mechanical design experience on high-complexity electromechanical products
